screen.question: Which named ligand-receptor-cell context provides the strongest auditable first target for a time-resolved, consumptive MEHLISSA capillary-tissue-cell coupling?
screen.selection_boundary: Public articles, supporting information, repositories, exact revisions, file hashes, licences, units, and time-resolved observations were screened. No third-party code or data are bundled, no dynamic equations or acceptance limits are selected, no model output has been inspected, and no biological, pulmonary, patient, or clinical qualification is claimed.

criteria.description: The candidate names one ligand, receptor system, primary cellular context, and dynamic trafficking or consumption response.
The publication, model, code, and data can be identified by persistent locator, immutable revision, or content hash.
Source amounts, concentrations, volumes, surfaces, times, and rates are explicit enough for a prospective SI conversion.
Time-resolved observations exist for the selected ligand-receptor process and their calibration or validation role can be declared.
Rights for articles, supporting information, data, and executable code are assessed independently rather than inferred from access.
A separately authored measurement family can challenge at least one dynamic behavior without refitting.
The represented species, cell type, preparation, and physiological state support a pulmonary-capillary interpretation.
A reduced MEHLISSA-native reference can be specified without importing a complete third-party platform or widening the claim.

candidates.name: Sarabipour 2025 VEGF-A165a-VEGFR2-NRP1 ligand-responsive trafficking in HUVECs

biology.ligand: human vascular endothelial growth factor A isoform 165a (VEGF-A165a)
biology.cell_type: primary human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs)
biology.preparation: confluent serum-starved endothelial cell culture exposed to exogenous ligand
biology.dynamic_response: ligand binding, surface loss, internalization into Rab4/5 and Rab11 compartments, recycling, and degradation
biology.physiological_scope: human endothelial in vitro mechanism; not lung-specific, in vivo, patient-specific, or clinical

publication.citation: Sarabipour S, Kinghorn K, Quigley KM, et al. Impact of ligand binding on VEGFR1, VEGFR2, and NRP1 localization in human endothelial cells. PLOS Computational Biology. 2025;21(7):e1013254.
publication.article_and_supporting_information_right: CC-BY-4.0 with attribution; the paper states that all manuscript data are in the Supporting Information

artifacts.role: model parameters, compartment geometry, binding and trafficking definitions
artifacts.path: S12 Table and linked S14-S18 tables

artifacts.role: auditable full BioNetGen reference, not a source to copy
auditable generated MATLAB reference, not a source to copy
repository copy of Figure 2C whole-cell time series; use the CC-BY Supporting Information as the rights-bearing source
artifacts.path: Liganded Trafficking 2025/R code/Figure 2 data and fig files/Fig2C_data.csv

artifacts.role: repository copy of Figure 2G one-hour surface, internal, and total measurements
artifacts.path: Liganded Trafficking 2025/R code/Figure 2 data and fig files/Fig2G_data.csv

artifacts.role: repository copy of Figure 2H four-hour surface, internal, and total measurements
artifacts.path: Liganded Trafficking 2025/R code/Figure 2 data and fig files/Fig2H_data.csv

unit_assessment.source_volume: femtolitres per represented cell, including 1e7 fL extracellular, 11.25 fL Rab4/5, and 3.75 fL Rab11
unit_assessment.source_surface: square micrometres per represented cell, including 1000 um2 cell surface, 950 um2 Rab4/5, and 325 um2 Rab11
unit_assessment.source_rates: first-order rates in s^-1 and association rates adjusted to molecules-per-cell, local volume, or local surface
unit_assessment.stimulus: 50 ng/mL VEGF-A165a is encoded as 6843182 molecules per represented cell for the source extracellular volume
required_dccq_1_3_decisions: freeze molecule-to-mole conversion using an explicit Avogadro constant
freeze the represented cell count and extracellular tissue volume
freeze the VEGF-A165a molecular-mass and monomer-versus-dimer convention
derive rather than silently reuse every adjusted association rate

candidates.data_role: The 2025 HUVEC observations may select the mechanism, calibration values, transformations, and observation model. They cannot validate the resulting candidate because they belong to the same evidence family.
strengths: Names a human endothelial ligand, receptor, coreceptor, cell preparation, and time-resolved trafficking response.
The article and Supporting Information are CC-BY-4.0 and provide explicit parameters, compartment geometry, and experimental observations.
The cited public repository can be pinned to one commit and its relevant files content-hashed.
Source units are explicit and can be mapped prospectively to the MEHLISSA SI amount ledger.
limitations: HUVEC culture is not human pulmonary capillary endothelium and does not establish resting lung physiology.
The full 281-state reference is larger than the first bounded MEHLISSA coupling should be.
The GitHub repository contains no explicit LICENSE, COPYING, or NOTICE file, so its code and standalone CSV files must not be copied, modified, or redistributed under an assumed licence.
A condition-matched, source-disjoint HUVEC time series has not yet been frozen for validation.
candidates.next_action: DCCQ-1.3 must independently specify a reduced MEHLISSA-native VEGF-A165a-VEGFR2 binding, internalization, recycling, and degradation model from the CC-BY publication record, freeze the SI mapping and observation roles, and retain NRP1 as an explicit included or excluded structural choice before output.

candidates.name: Clegg and Mac Gabhann 2015 VEGFR2 trafficking and site-specific phosphorylation model

biology.cell_type: HUVEC and porcine aortic endothelial-cell evidence contexts
biology.preparation: endothelial monolayer exposed to soluble or matrix-bound ligand
biology.dynamic_response: binding, endosomal trafficking, degradation, recycling, and site-specific VEGFR2 phosphorylation
biology.physiological_scope: endothelial in vitro mechanism; not lung-specific or patient-specific

publication.citation: Clegg LW, Mac Gabhann F. Site-Specific Phosphorylation of VEGFR2 Is Mediated by Receptor Trafficking: Insights from a Computational Model. PLOS Computational Biology. 2015;11(6):e1004158.

artifacts.role: complete biochemical and trafficking reaction reference

unit_assessment.source_amount: explicit molecule and concentration definitions by study
unit_assessment.source_volume: extracellular, surface, Rab4/5, Rab11, and degraded compartments
unit_assessment.source_rates: binding, trafficking, and phosphorylation parameters are tabulated with units
required_dccq_1_3_decisions: reconstruct only if the selected 2025 target proves unsuitable
separate trafficking from phosphorylation to preserve the first bounded scope

candidates.data_role: Useful structural and mechanistic reference for the reduced equation set; it is not source-disjoint from the selected Mac Gabhann laboratory evidence family.
strengths: Provides a detailed endothelial VEGFR2 and NRP1 trafficking mechanism with explicit parameter tables.
The article and Supporting Information are CC-BY-4.0.
It connects trafficking to receptor phosphorylation and therefore provides a later feedback extension path.
limitations: No exact licensed executable source artifact was established in this screen.
The 97-species and phosphorylation-rich model is larger than the minimum dynamic coupling target.
It shares scientific lineage with the selected source and cannot serve as source-disjoint validation.
candidates.next_action: Use as a structural reference in DCCQ-1.3 and as a fallback only if the selected source cannot support a reduced, prospectively specified implementation.

candidates.name: Kuehn and Checa 2019 AngioABM VEGFR1-VEGFR2-Dll4-Notch sprouting model

biology.dynamic_response: VEGF diffusion and uptake, VEGFR1/VEGFR2 signaling, Dll4-Notch lateral inhibition, migration, and sprouting
biology.physiological_scope: developmental mouse sprouting model; not normal human pulmonary capillary physiology

publication.citation: Kuehn C, Checa S. Computational Modeling to Quantify the Contributions of VEGFR1, VEGFR2, and Lateral Inhibition in Sprouting Angiogenesis. Frontiers in Physiology. 2019;10:288.

artifacts.role: AngioABM simulation engine and VEGFR1 study configuration

unit_assessment.source_amount: agent and lattice variables with model-specific scaling
unit_assessment.source_volume: two-dimensional lattice rather than the DCCQ amount-volume ledger
unit_assessment.source_rates: intracellular and uptake parameters include model-specific factors such as uptake_factor
required_dccq_1_3_decisions: do not import the agent platform for the first DCCQ coupling
use only separately justified reaction concepts if needed

candidates.data_role: Licensed reproducibility and multicellular angiogenesis alternative; not a source for normal human endothelial or pulmonary-capillary parameterization.
strengths: Exact immutable VEGFR1 tags now exist for both repositories even though the publication's same-named branches no longer do.
The code is explicitly Apache-2.0 and combines VEGF uptake with endothelial receptor signaling.
It provides a later multicellular sprouting benchmark.
limitations: The biological context is mouse embryoid-body sprouting rather than human pulmonary or quiescent capillary endothelium.
The platform is a large two-dimensional agent-based model with model-specific units and high integration cost.
The publication-stated BioModels submission MODEL1804030001 was not established as a currently released public model artifact.
candidates.next_action: Retain for a later angiogenesis package; do not use it to define the first DCCQ SI tissue-receptor boundary.

biology.physiological_scope: average HeLa cell; not endothelial, pulmonary, or patient-specific

artifacts.role: cell-solver regression and evidence-governance reference only

unit_assessment.source_volume: not mapped to an SI tissue volume
required_dccq_1_3_decisions: do not vary or reinterpret the BCQ input

candidates.data_role: Existing computational regression; not a dynamic endothelial evidence source.
strengths: Already computationally qualified across COPASI and the MEHLISSA implementation.
Useful as a regression for solver, provenance, and evidence-governance behavior.
limitations: Wrong ligand, receptor, and cell context for the endothelial coupling target.
The fixed source stimulus and unresolved model-native units block a direct SI dynamic boundary.
The qualified result is an average-cell computational claim, not biological or pulmonary qualification.
candidates.next_action: Keep unchanged as a BCQ regression; do not connect it to the DCCQ capillary ledger.

decision.selected_target: human VEGF-A165a to VEGFR2 ligand binding and trafficking in primary HUVECs, with NRP1 treated as an explicit structural choice
decision.selection_reason: The selected family provides the best combined human endothelial fit, exact publication and repository identity, explicit molecule-per-cell, time, volume, surface, and rate units, reusable CC-BY Supporting Information, and time-resolved observations. Its repository licence gap, non-pulmonary cell origin, and source-disjoint context mismatch remain explicit blockers rather than being averaged away by the score.
authorized_for_dccq_1_3: use the CC-BY publication and Supporting Information to specify an independent reduced MEHLISSA-native model
freeze an SI amount, volume, area, concentration, and rate conversion before any dynamic output
assign the 2024 and 2025 HUVEC family only to mechanism selection, parameterization, and within-study checks
reserve Peach 2019 for a source-disjoint kinetic challenge with an explicit cell-context mismatch
reserve Zhao 2010 for a source-disjoint directional HUVEC check only
not_yet_authorized: copying, modifying, bundling, or redistributing code or CSV files from the unlicensed VEGFR-Trafficking-Projects repository
selecting equations, state reductions, parameters, tolerances, observation transformations, or validation exclusions after viewing MEHLISSA outputs
calling the source family a pulmonary, in vivo, patient-specific, biological-validation, or clinical result
marking DCCQ-G1 or DCCQ-G7 passed before the SI map and exact no-refit observation protocol are frozen and executed

gate_implications.DCCQ-G1: PARTIAL: one chemical identity and a convertible source unit system are selected, but the SI mapping and represented cell-volume convention remain to be frozen in DCCQ-1.3.
gate_implications.DCCQ-G6: PARTIAL: measurement variability and parameter sources exist, but distributions, correlations, identifiability rules, and uncertainty propagation remain to be frozen.
gate_implications.DCCQ-G7: BLOCKED: source-disjoint kinetic and directional observations are identified, but no condition-matched independent HUVEC time series and no prospective numeric evaluation protocol are frozen.
gate_implications.DCCQ-G8: BLOCKED: no implementation, result archive, or close-out review exists.

decision.allowed_current_claim: DCCQ-1.2 selects and machine-checks a human endothelial VEGF-A165a-VEGFR2-NRP1 target and evidence family for prospective model definition. It establishes source identity, unit convertibility, data roles, and rights boundaries; it does not implement or qualify dynamic coupling.
decision.next_increment: DCCQ-1.3 prospective reduced equations, SI mapping, synchronization, and evaluation protocol
